name: Vansen ChemShell Acid-Rated Coverall Pro
description: Vansen's ChemShell is a Circuit-tier staple — a single-piece coverall in flat industrial yellow with black chemical-resistance rating stripes across the chest and thighs. The outer shell is thermoplastic-bonded polyaramid, stiff at the shoulders but articulated at the elbows and knees with accordion gussets. Seams are triple-welded and color-coded by rating class. A chest pocket holds a folded decon wipe sleeve. The hood is detachable via quarter-turn collar locks. Finish is matte and scuffs to a worn sheen after a few shifts.
functionality: Rated for concentrated sulfuric, hydrochloric, and nitric acid splash exposure. Integrated nitrile wrist seals mate with compatible gauntlets. Decon-ready surface — low chemical absorption, wipe-clean exterior. Hood locks provide airtight collar seal when paired with a full-face respirator.
what_it_says: You follow the safety protocols because you've seen what happens when someone doesn't.
story_hooks: A Vansen ChemShell with a forged rating stripe — upgraded from Class B to Class A on paper — has been circulating in Circuit markets; the forgery is nearly undetectable.
The quarter-turn collar lock is also used as an improvised restraint mechanism by at least one known Shelf enforcer.
A worker survived a full chemical bath in this suit when a pipe burst — the suit was rated for splash, not immersion. It held anyway. Barely.
